newsitem.title: USA: Harken sees '98 exploration costs at $60 mln.
newsitem.headline: Harken sees '98 exploration costs at $60 mln.

text.p: Oil and gas exploration company Harken Energy Corp expects its 1998 oil exploration costs to come in between $60 and $65 million, up from about $44 million this year, a top Harken executive said.

"Next year our exploratory costs should be about $60 to $65 million," Bruce Huff, Harken's chief financial officer, said in response to a question after Harken's presentation at the American Stock Exchange Energy Conference in New York.
He declined to discuss the company's developmental costs.
Huff said that, in line with Harken's more speculative strategy in Colombia, the vast majority of exploratory costs will be made in that South American country.
He said just a few million will be spent on U.S. exploration in 1998, down from $7-$8 million this year.

During an earlier official presentation, Huff and Harken Chairman Mikel Faulkner stressed that dependable production from mature U.S. fields was central to sustaining the company's more risky strategy in Colombia.
"We have the domestic side to support our drilling as we look for that major find in Colombia," Faulkner told analysts during the company's presentation.

In terms of acreage contracted to be explored, Harken is the number three foreign presence in Colombia behind majors British Petroleum Co Plc and Amoco Inc, with a million acres contracted to be explored.
Its domestic presence is in "sunbelt" states Texas, Arizona, New Mexico, Arkansas and Utah where it has over 10 million barrels of oil equivalent in proven reserves.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Oil Desk 1 212 859 1633
